subject: Dedicated capacity queueing differential waiver request - HeliosAI pilot
messages:
From: Max Turner <max.turner@heliosai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-20 13:04:00 -0400
Subject: Request: dedicated capacity queueing differential waiver

Hi Priyom,

Quick note from our ops/procurement side — we're about to convert a research-grade workload into a regulated inference pipeline and need some confirmation on the Dedicated capacity behavior. During peak windows our batch fan-in spikes by ~3x for short intervals (2–7 minutes). With reserved GPUs alone, the default queueing rules cause our tail latency to exceed our compliance window.

Two asks:
- Is there a documented path to request a temporary queueing differential / headroom carveout for a reserved pool (we'd like a 30% carveout for scheduled daily peaks for the first 90 days of go-live)?
- If so, what monitoring/guardrails do you require from our side to safely grant that? Our infra team exported recent peak patterns (attached).

We're in a procurement timeline and would prefer to fold any carveout into the Dedicated contract amendment rather than a separate SLA exception. Happy to jump on a quick call.

Thanks,
Max Turner
Head of Platform
HeliosAI

Attachments: helios_peak_metrics_202705-202706.csv (CSV)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Max Turner <max.turner@heliosai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity queueing differential waiver

Hi Max — thanks for the context and the metrics, that's helpful. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Karthik (dedicated runtime) so we can propose an operational approach.

High level: we can support a time-bound queueing differential for a reserved pool, but it needs two things up front:
1) A clear schedule (daily start/stop windows) and a maximum tolerated peak multiplier.
2) An observability contract: token-level latency histograms and earliest/last request traces during the carveout windows so our on-call can act quickly if we see tail regressions.

Proposed next step from our side: we draft a 90-day pilot amendment that includes a 30% headroom carveout for the contracted pool, automated telemetry feeds to a shared SLO dashboard, and an automatic rollback trigger if 95th-percentile latency crosses the agreed threshold for >10 minutes. Can you confirm if Helios can provide the telemetry stream (Prometheus/Grafana or S3 telemetry dump) and the preferred daily window?

We'll also run this past legal — tagging Olga on the amendment language.

— Priyom
Senior Manager, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: recommendation for HeliosAI carveout (draft talking points)

Team — internal notes / proposed terms to include in the amendment:  

- Scope: apply to dedicated pool "Helios-P1" (32 reserved GPUs) for an initial 90-day pilot following first production traffic date.
- Headroom: allow scheduled daily windows (local TZ) up to 30% additional concurrent inflight requests above reserved concurrency for a maximum of 10 minutes per occurrence, 6 occurrences per day.
- SLOs: target 95th-percentile token latency <150ms during normal hours; carveout accepted if 95p latency remains <300ms during declared windows.
- Rollback: automated fallback to normal queueing if 95p crosses 300ms for >10 consecutive minutes or if error rate delta >0.5%.
- Observability: Helios to forward token-level latency histograms (per-minute) to our ingestion endpoint and provide a daily summary CSV.
- Credits: if rollback is triggered, customer receives a blended credit equal to 7 days of reserved pool usage prorated.

Karthik — are these engineering-feasible w/ current Dedicated runtime? I recommend we keep the initial pilot conservative and instrument aggressively. Olga, please prepare amendment language and a short redline. Marissa, I'll hand over the negotiation cadence once legal confirms.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: Max Turner <max.turner@heliosai.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@heliosai.com>
Date: 2027-06-24 11:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity queueing differential waiver

Priyom / team — appreciate the quick reply and the concrete terms. A few clarifications from procurement/engineering:

- We can provide a Prometheus pushgateway feed with per-minute histograms and a daily CSV export.
- The daily windows we need are 08:00–09:00 and 18:30–19:00 PT; those cover scheduled model refresh traffic.
- Helios must maintain 95p tail <300ms during carveout windows; the 150ms baseline is ambitious for our current model size but the 300ms ceiling during carveout is acceptable.
- One ask: can Redwood guarantee that credits are automatic (applied without requiring a claims process) if rollback triggers are hit? Procurement prefers automated credits to speed reconciliations.

We're happy to run the 90-day pilot. Please send a draft amendment (PDF) and a DocuSign link; procurement needs the DocuSign record in our contract management system.

Regards,
Max Turner
Head of Platform, HeliosAI

Attachments: proposed-amendment-draft.pdf (PDF)
From: priyom_das@redwood.com

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Request: dedicated capacity queueing differential waiver

Max — great, thanks for confirming windows and telemetry. We're aligned on the terms. Next steps:

1) Legal note: Olga is preparing an amendment that binds the 90-day pilot, the automatic crediting mechanism, and the rollback triggers. We'll send a redline by EOD tomorrow.
2) Engineering note: Karthik will create a read-only ingestion endpoint for your Prometheus push so metrics flow into our SLO dashboard. I'll share the endpoint and auth details in a separate secure message.
3) Procurement/admin: I created the deal record and assigned an internal ID: DL-2027-0957. We'll push a DocuSign link in the next 24 hours: https://docusign.net/HeliosAI/SLA-Amendment-0957

If these match your expectations, we'll proceed with signatures and schedule the pilot start for 2027-07-05.

— Priyom
Senior Manager, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference
